SECRET

Copies in: FF.PP.2573
158/1424

PP.48,763/D.I.A./BRJ. 25 October, 1954
S1/16204/8.

Headquarters,
British Services Security Organisation,
B.A.O.R. 12.

Dr. Wilhela Wolfgang SCHULTZ

Please refer to your letter of 15 October, 1954, about SCHULTZ. We have a record of Dr. Helmuth Von RAUSCHENFALT who changed his name to Fritz RENNARD in approximately 1946 when he returned to Germany from the U.K.

Our records show that he was born in Dresden on 2 October 1896 and that he is a Doctor of political economy. He first came to this country in 1928 and was exempted from internment during the war because of the useful work he was doing for P.W.E., Ministry of Information and the B.B.C. Planning Committee.

Von RAUSCHENFALT was regarded as a moderate Socialist intellectual (I.S.K.) until 1942, when he left their ranks as a result of some unspecified division from the I.S.K. policy. Also in 1942, P.W.E. decided not to renew his contract because they "felt uneasy" about him although there was "nothing definite against him".

He is believed to have done research work for the Fabian Society and the Workers Education Association during the period 1942 - 1944. In 1944 he was vetted for employment by O.S.S. but it is not known whether he was ever taken on by them. In an application for a U.S. visa dated 1950, he stated that he had been an independent writer in the period 1942 - 1945.

While there was some suspicion that Von RAUSCHENFALT's sympathies lay further to the left than those of the moderate Socialist intellectuals with whom he identified himself while in Germany and later in the U.K. until 1942, there is no evidence of his having been a member of the Communist Party or having given expression to Communist sympathies.

With reference to GERBER; we have a record of a Karl Johannes GERBER, born on 22 January 1895 in Elberfeld, who visited the U.K. on a number of occasions between 1933 and the beginning of the war. In the spring of 1940 he was arrested in Belgium and handed over to the French, who sent him to an internment camp in the Pyrenees. He was eventually released and entered the United States at New York in March 1941. He became a naturalised citizen of the U.S. in 1947, since when we have no further information about him.

He was not in the U.K. during the war years and came to our notice solely as a result of his association and correspondence with the infamous Aleister CROWLEY, the mystic and black magician. GERBER was evidently one of CROWLEY's converts and most enthusiastic supporters.
